newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai authorities dress Thai finance wounds.
newsitem.headline: Thai authorities dress Thai finance wounds.

text.p: The Thai government announced measures on Saturday aimed at furthering efforts made last week to assure investors it would restore calm and stability to the beleaguered financial sector.
Officials announced concrete measures aimed at bailing out troubled property developers and their creditors during a meeting of financial executives at this coastal resort town.

The central bank said the Bank of Thailand plans to issue zero coupon bonds to raise up to 100 billion baht ($3.8 billion) with which to buy sub-standard assets from property developers, finance firms and banks.

"The bonds will boost the liquidity of finance companies and the cash flows of property developers to help them gradually trim their inventory of unsold projects," Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said.
Rerngchai said he expected the Thai cabinet this week to approve the issuance of the bonds.
Deteriorating loan quality, caused by a four-year slump in the local property market and slowing economic growth, has caused severe liquidity problems in the financial sector.

The central bank took the unprecedented step of suspending share trading in finance and bank stocks last Monday while it identified 10 struggling finance firms and announced stringent new measures designed to shore up the ailing financial sector.
It ordered the 10 to raise capital and instructed all banks and finance companies to set aside higher provisions for sub-standard assets.
The bank said commercial banks and finance companies will need to reserve a combined 50 billion baht of additional funds in order to meet the higher provision requirements.

The measures triggered several days of public runs on deposits at many of Thailand's 91 finance companies. The public withdrawals eased on Friday after the central bank assured the public that it would guarantee repayment of all promissory notes issued by finance firms.

Rerngchai and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Saturday they expect to see some finance company mergers in the near future which will help strengthen firms faced with an increasingly competitive environment.
"We will use carrot and stick to induce mergers of finance companies by giving incentives to those who agree to merge, including increasing the scope of their licensed business," Rerngchai said.
Amnuay said the authorities would continue to act decisively to contain problems in the finance sector.
"We have to take the pain in order to prevent death in the future ... if we need to perform surgery, we should do it," he said.
"The authorities will come up with more measures which will not necessarily be bitter pills, some will be sweet pills like the zero coupon bonds," Rerngchai said. ($1 = 26 baht)
